pharm: Locally acting stimulant laxative that increases colonic motility and intestinal fluid secretion to produce a bowel movement
quick: Oral 5-15 mg once daily; rectal 10 mg once daily
Take whole; do not take within 1 h of antacids/milk
Generally considered acceptable; use if needed
summary: Bisacodyl is a stimulant (contact) laxative used for short-term relief of occasional constipation and for bowel cleansing before procedures. Oral tablets are enteric-coated and act in 6-12 hours, while rectal suppositories act within 15-60 minutes. It stimulates colonic peristalsis and increases fluid and electrolyte secretion into the bowel. It should be used short term; chronic or excessive use can cause electrolyte disturbance, fluid loss and laxative dependence. Tablets must be swallowed whole and not taken within 1 hour of antacids or dairy products.
indications: Short-term relief of occasional constipation and irregularity
Bowel evacuation before surgery, radiologic procedures or endoscopy
Constipation in conditions requiring a soft stool

dosage.d: 5-15 mg (usually 1-3 tablets) as a single daily dose
dosage.n: Produces a bowel movement in 6-12 h

dosage.d: Per procedure protocol (often combined with other agents)

admin: Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush, split or chew (enteric-coated)
Do not take tablets within 1 hour of antacids, milk or other dairy products
Insert suppository fully into the rectum, pointed end first
Use for short-term relief only; do not use for more than about 1 week without medical advice
moa: After hydrolysis to its active metabolite (BHPM) by intestinal enzymes, bisacodyl directly stimulates the colonic mucosa and enteric nerves to increase peristalsis, and promotes accumulation of water and electrolytes in the colonic lumen, producing a laxative effect.

absolute: Rectal bleeding or anal fissure/proctitis (for suppository)
relative: Symptoms such as abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting
Sudden change in bowel habit lasting >2 weeks
monitor: Fluid and electrolyte status with prolonged use

preg: Generally considered acceptable for short-term use because systemic absorption is minimal; use only if needed and prefer dietary/bulk measures first. Consult a clinician.
lact: Compatible with breastfeeding; minimal systemic absorption and the active metabolite is not detected in breast milk in significant amounts.
renal: No specific dose adjustment, but avoid prolonged or excessive use that could cause fluid and electrolyte loss.

moderate: Diuretics or corticosteroids - additive risk of hypokalemia with overuse
Cardiac glycosides (digoxin) - hypokalemia increases toxicity risk
Antacids / milk / H2 blockers / PPIs - premature dissolution of enteric tablet causing gastric irritation
interactions.food: Do not take enteric-coated tablets within 1 hour of milk or dairy
interactions.diagnostics: Excessive use may cause hypokalemia affecting ECG and electrolyte panels

serious: Fluid and electrolyte disturbance (hypokalemia) with overuse
Laxative dependence and atonic colon with chronic misuse
rare: Proctitis or rectal bleeding with suppositories

monitoring: Fluid and electrolyte balance if used beyond a few days
counsel: Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew
Do not take within 1 hour of milk, dairy or antacids
Drink plenty of fluids and use for short-term relief only
Stop and see a doctor if you have rectal bleeding or no bowel movement after use
Do not use if you have stomach pain, nausea or vomiting
Tablets work in 6-12 hours; suppositories in 15-60 minutes
pk: Minimal systemic absorption; local colonic action
Active metabolite ~16 h (largely not systemically active)
Below 25-30 C; store suppositories below 30 C, avoid heat
pearls: Enteric-coated tablets must be swallowed whole and kept away from antacids/dairy
Rectal suppository acts much faster (within an hour) than oral tablets
For short-term use only; chronic misuse causes hypokalemia and an atonic colon
Minimal systemic absorption makes it acceptable in pregnancy and lactation
Hypokalemia from overuse can potentiate digoxin toxicity
missed: Used as needed for constipation; if a scheduled dose is missed, take it when remembered, but do not take extra doses to make up.
overdose: Overuse or overdose causes diarrhea, abdominal cramps, dehydration and electrolyte loss (notably hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia), which may lead to muscle weakness and cardiac effects. Management is supportive with fluid and electrolyte replacement; there is no specific antidote.
